speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to begin my assessment, how long has this lesion been present, and have you noticed any changes in its size or appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and the rapid development of a painful ulcer at a site of minor trauma (ant bite) with no signs of infection, this presentation is highly characteristic of Pyoderma Gangrenosum. Have you noticed any systemic symptoms like fever or increased fatigue?
